title: Inside a Pipe Organ
description: Explore organ pipes, keyboards, and airflow through directly defined parts of a large musical instrument.
cardDescription: Explore organ pipes, keyboards, and airflow through directly defined parts of a large musical instrument.
focus: An organ's keys control air reaching pipes; it does not make sound by striking piano strings.
solvingTip: The shortest airflow words help cross the longer instrument parts.
words: Keyboard instrument that can sound ranks of air-driven pipes
Keyboard played by the hands on an organ
Foot-operated keyboard beneath an organ console
Control selecting a set or type of organ pipes
Device supplying or regulating air for an organ
Sounding tube in an acoustic organ
Moving gas that makes an organ pipe sound
Lever pressed by an organist's finger
Set of organ pipes sharing a tonal character
Playing station containing an organ's keyboards and controls
Building often housing a large pipe organ
Low musical range often played with organ pedals
Several notes sounded together on the organ

answerNotes.ORGAN: A pipe organ uses moving air, unlike an electronic instrument imitating its sound.
answerNotes.MANUAL: Manual distinguishes a hand keyboard from the pedalboard.
answerNotes.PEDALBOARD: The organist's feet can play a separate musical part.
answerNotes.STOP: Stops change the available sound by controlling which pipes receive air.
answerNotes.BELLOWS: Traditional organs used bellows; modern installations commonly include electric blowers.

title: A Piano Tuner's Visit
description: Follow a piano tuner through the tuning lever, strings, and quiet comparison of pitches.
cardDescription: Follow a piano tuner through the tuning lever, strings, and quiet comparison of pitches.
focus: Tuning changes string tension; it is different from repairing a worn key or hammer action.
solvingTip: Read whether a clue asks for a tool, a sound, or an adjustment.
words: Person adjusting piano strings to their intended pitches
Special tool used to turn a piano's tuning pins
Metal fitting turned to change a piano string's tension
Pulling force changed when a piano string is tuned
Same pitch sounded by several piano strings for one note
Taut wire producing a piano tone when struck
Soft wedge used to silence neighboring strings during tuning
How high or low a piano note sounds
Pulsing heard when two nearly equal pitches sound together
Body part used to listen for tuning differences
Implement carried in the visiting tuner's case
Piano lever pressed to test a note
Interval spanning eight letter-name steps in a scale
Room condition helping the tuner listen carefully

answerNotes.TUNER: A tuner listens and measures while changing the tension of strings.
answerNotes.LEVER: A tuning lever is sometimes called a tuning hammer, but it does not strike the strings.
answerNotes.PIN: The tuning pin holds the adjusted string tension.
answerNotes.TENSION: Changing tension changes pitch when other string properties stay the same.
answerNotes.UNISON: Many piano notes use more than one string sounding together.

title: Taking Turns in a Piano Duet
description: Share a piano bench through two players, four hands, and the page turns of a simple duet.
cardDescription: Share a piano bench through two players, four hands, and the page turns of a simple duet.
subtheme: Taking Turns in a Piano Duet
focus: A duet involves two performers. At one piano, they can sit side by side and follow separate parts.
solvingTip: Short number and direction words help cross the music terms.
words: Musical performance shared by two players
Other person sharing the piano performance
Number of hands used by two pianists together
Long seat that two piano players may share
One side of the sheet music turned during the duet
Move from one sheet-music page to the next
Take a place on the piano bench
Body part resting on the piano keys
Direction opposite right along the keyboard
Direction opposite left along the keyboard
At the same time, as partners play a duet
Friendly expression between the two piano partners
Use the bench with another player
Signal helping the two players begin together

answerNotes.DUET: A duet counts two performers rather than two notes sounding together.
answerNotes.PARTNER: The partner plays alongside the first player rather than merely listening.
answerNotes.FOUR: Four hands is a familiar description for two people at one piano.
answerNotes.BENCH: A bench provides a place to sit, not a stand for the printed music.
answerNotes.PAGE: A page turn moves the players to the next part of the printed music.

title: Watching a Player Piano
description: Recall a player piano through its paper roll, moving keys, foot pedals, and familiar tune.
cardDescription: Recall a player piano through its paper roll, moving keys, foot pedals, and familiar tune.
focus: Holes in the moving paper tell a traditional player piano which notes to play. No technical mechanism names are needed for these clues.
solvingTip: Try an ordinary material or body-part word first.
words: Word before piano for an instrument operated by a paper roll
Long strip of music paper wound around a spool
Small opening in the music paper that helps select a note
Cylinder around which the piano's paper is wound
Foot lever used on some traditional player pianos
Material carrying the music roll's punched openings
White or black lever that may move as the roll plays
Seat in front of the old piano
Moving gas used inside a traditional player-piano mechanism
Familiar tune heard as the paper roll moves
Rotate, as a spool does while the music plays
Body part used to press a piano pedal
Change position, as the keys do during a tune

answerNotes.PLAYER: A player piano follows instructions encoded in the moving paper.
answerNotes.ROLL: The roll stores instructions, rather than a microphone recording of sound.
answerNotes.HOLE: Patterns of holes tell the mechanism which notes to sound.
answerNotes.SPOOL: A spool holds the paper as it moves through the instrument.
answerNotes.PEDAL: The player can use foot pedals to supply power to an air-driven mechanism.

description: Explore a home keyboard through its selected sounds, speakers, power supply, and rhythm controls.
cardDescription: Explore a home keyboard through its selected sounds, speakers, power supply, and rhythm controls.
focus: An electronic keyboard produces sound electronically; its keys need not operate physical strings.
solvingTip: The familiar controls provide short answers around the longer instrument words.
words: Portable electronic instrument with piano-like keys
Stored sound or setting selected with a button
Part converting the keyboard's electrical signal into audible sound
External power supply plugged into some keyboards
Pattern supplied by an automatic backing feature
White or black lever played with a finger
Control setting the instrument's output loudness
Support holding the portable instrument at playing height
Stored group of sounds or settings
Selectable instrument sound on many electronic keyboards

Regular pulse in the automatic accompaniment

answerNotes.KEYBOARD: A keyboard can offer many sounds without containing the corresponding acoustic instruments.
answerNotes.PRESET: A preset recalls a prepared configuration instead of building one from scratch.
answerNotes.SPEAKER: Speakers produce the sound heard outside the instrument.
answerNotes.ADAPTER: Some keyboards can also use batteries; power arrangements vary.
answerNotes.RHYTHM: An automatic rhythm can provide a steady accompaniment for practice.
